gold.user: As a project manager, I want to retrieve all custom fields in my Jira instance to understand what data can be captured.
gold.ideal: A successful response with a list of all custom fields, including their IDs, names, and types.

gold.user: As a product owner, I want to create a new custom field for tracking user feedback in my project.
gold.ideal: A successful response indicating the custom field has been created, along with its ID and details.

gold.user: As a developer, I need to fetch custom fields in a paginated manner to efficiently handle large datasets.
gold.ideal: A successful response with a paginated list of custom fields, including metadata for pagination.

gold.user: As a system administrator, I want to view all trashed custom fields to decide which ones to restore or permanently delete.
gold.ideal: A successful response with a list of trashed custom fields, including their IDs and names.

gold.user: As a project lead, I want to update the configuration of an existing custom field to better suit our project needs.
gold.ideal: A successful response confirming that the custom field has been updated with the new configuration.

gold.user: As a business analyst, I want to retrieve the contexts associated with a specific custom field to understand its usage.
gold.ideal: A successful response with a list of contexts for the specified custom field.

gold.user: As a product manager, I want to delete a custom field that is no longer needed to keep our project clean.
gold.ideal: A successful response confirming that the custom field has been deleted.

gold.user: As a system administrator, I want to restore a previously deleted custom field because it is still relevant to our project.
gold.ideal: A successful response indicating that the custom field has been restored.

gold.user: As a project coordinator, I want to trash a custom field that is no longer in use to prevent it from cluttering our field list.
gold.ideal: A successful response confirming that the custom field has been moved to trash.
